summary.text: Gondwana was a large landmass, commonly described as a supercontinent, whose remnants make up around two-thirds of today's continental area.
Those remnants include South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, Zealandia, Arabia and the Indian subcontinent, and at its largest it covered about one-fifth of Earth's surface.
It fused with Laurasia to form Pangaea during the Carboniferous, then separated and began breaking into pieces in the Early Jurassic, around 180 million years ago.

facts.label: Built from
facts.value: Fragments of the older supercontinent Rodinia

facts.label: Final break-up
facts.value: Antarctica split from South America and Australia

items.prompt: Gondwana's leftover pieces are still on the map today. Roughly how much of today's continental area do they make up?
items.explain: The remnants of Gondwana, including South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia and India, make up around two-thirds of today's continental area.

items.prompt: Several of today's continents are leftovers of Gondwana. Which one is not among them?
items.explain: Gondwana's remnants include South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, Zealandia, Arabia and the Indian subcontinent; North America is not on that list.

items.prompt: A botanist finds closely related plant groups in South America, Africa and Australia, though wide oceans now separate them. What best explains this?

options.label: The lands were once one landmass
The plants evolved by pure chance

items.explain: Regions that were part of Gondwana shared plants and animals, and some of those shared elements persist today.

items.prompt: Gondwana's name means 'forest of the Gonds' and was borrowed from a real region. In which country is that region?
items.explain: Eduard Suess named it after an Indian region whose Sanskrit name means 'forest of the Gonds'.

items.prompt: Gondwana later joined another huge landmass to form the supercontinent Pangaea. Which landmass was that?
items.explain: Gondwana fused with Laurasia during the Carboniferous to form Pangaea.

items.prompt: The last stage of Gondwana's break-up opened the Drake and Tasmanian Passages. Which continent was cut loose from South America and Australia?
items.explain: The final break-up split Antarctica from South America and Australia, forming the Drake and Tasmanian Passages.
